history.summary: DISTRICT CORRECTED: Jhalmala is in Balod district (Balod tehsil), not Durg district. Ganga Maiya is a famous Durga shrine at Jhalmala, 4 km east of Balod on the Durg-Balod road and 58 km from Durg. Legend: a fisherman's net repeatedly caught a Durga idol in the village pond; after a Gond tribal dreamed the goddess asking to be installed, the idol was placed in a kutcha hut and named Ganga Maiya since she came from water. Shri Bhikam Chand Tawri first gave it a temple shape; devotee donations later built the present complex, run by a trust that also organises cultural festivals and medical camps. It is a major Navratri pilgrimage: thousands throng here, some walking barefoot from long distances, in both the Chaitra and Ashwin Navratris. NOTE: the English Wikipedia page claims the temple 'was converted into the Catholic church dedicated to Saint Andrew' while retaining the temple structure — this conflicts with all other sources and is UNVERIFIED. Coordinates are from a single online place listing (verify on ground).

name: Ganga Maiya Temple, Jhalmala
town_description: Jhalmala is a village in Balod tehsil, Balod district, Chhattisgarh, about 4 km east of Balod town on the Durg-Balod main road and 58 km from Durg. It is best known for the Ganga Maiya Temple, one of the prime religious and pilgrim sites of the state, which the temple trust has developed into a green tourist spot with regular cultural and medical activities.
